comparisons.peer_summary: AMD faces potential intellectual property infringement claims from third parties that could result in substantial damages, injunctions stopping product sales, or costly licensing and redesign efforts, any of which could have a material adverse effect on the business.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose risks related to intellectual property infringement litigation, specifically noting exposure through indemnification obligations to customers. MU states it is subject to claims including IP infringement and obligations to defend customers against third-party IP claims (S001-S002, S004). Similarly, AMD discloses that third parties may bring actions alleging IP infringement by AMD or its customers, and notes the potential for injunctions or damages if such claims are asserted (S001, S004). Both highlight the direct link between being sued and defending customer sales.

sentences.text: From time to time, we are subject to various legal, regulatory and administrative investigations, inquiries, proceedings, and claims that arise out of the ordinary conduct of our business or otherwise, both domestically and internationally.
Such claims, investigations, inquiries, and proceedings may include, but are not limited to, allegations of anticompetitive conduct and infringement of intellectual property.

• our indemnification obligations, including obligations to defend our customers against third-party claims asserting infringement of certain intellectual property rights, which may include patents, trademarks, copyrights, or trade secrets; and

With respect to intellectual property litigation, from time to time, we have been notified of, or third parties may bring or have brought, actions against us and/or against our customers based on allegations that we are infringing the intellectual property rights of others, contributing to or inducing the infringement of the intellectual property rights of others, improperly claiming ownership of intellectual property or otherwise improperly using the intellectual property of others.

These parties may file lawsuits against us or our customers seeking damages (potentially up to and including treble damages) or an injunction against the sale of products that incorporate allegedly infringed intellectual property or against the operation of our business as presently conducted, which could result in our having to stop the sale of some of our products or to increase the costs of selling some of our products or which could damage our reputation.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD is a party to various legal actions, including securities, corporate governance, consumer class actions, product liability, and environmental claims from former manufacturing facilities. Outcomes are uncertain, and successful claims could result in material damages, substantial costs, or prohibitions on selling products.
comparisons.comparison: MU and AMD both identify product warranties as a source of potential litigation and liability. MU explicitly lists 'product warranties or from product liability claims' as a basis for associated litigation (S005). AMD similarly notes that its products are purchased by consumers, increasing exposure to 'consumer actions such as product liability claims and consumer class action claims' (S003). While both address the broader category of product-related legal risk, AMD specifically highlights consumer class actions, whereas MU groups it with general warranty liabilities.

sentences.text: • the terms of our product warranties or from product liability claims.
Our products are purchased by and/or used by consumers, which could increase our exposure to consumer actions such as product liability claims and consumer class action claims.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company faces warranty claims, product recalls, and product liability, with potential liabilities that may be significant, unlimited, and exceed revenue from relevant products. Reserves and insurance may be inadequate to cover uninsured portions of such claims, materially affecting financial condition.
comparisons.comparison: MU and AVGO both disclose significant exposure to warranty claims and product liability, emphasizing the potential for unlimited financial impact. MU notes it is subject to claims from product warranties and product liability (S005). AVGO elaborates that potential liabilities are 'significant, and in some cases... potentially unlimited' and that reserves or insurance may be inadequate to cover uninsured portions (P100_S003, P100_S008). Both companies acknowledge that product defects can lead to substantial legal and financial consequences.

sentences.text: • the terms of our product warranties or from product liability claims.
We are subject to warranty claims, product recalls and product liability.
The potential liabilities associated with such provisions are significant, and in some cases, including in agreements with some of our largest customers, are potentially unlimited.
Although we maintain reserves for reasonably estimable liabilities and purchase product liability insurance, our reserves may be inadequate to cover the uninsured portion of such claims.

comparisons.peer_topic: Intellectual Property Litigation Risks and Consequences
comparisons.peer_summary: Third parties, including non-practicing entities, assert IP claims against Intel, which can increase costs, disrupt operations, and harm reputation. Specific examples include an injunction obtained by R2 Semiconductor in Germany in February 2024 and adverse judgments in VLSI and R2 cases. IP claims may require Intel to pay damages, indemnify customers, stop manufacturing products, or enter costly license agreements, potentially harming its competitive position and requiring asset impairments.
comparisons.comparison: MU and INTC both disclose the risk of third-party intellectual property infringement claims and the associated costs. MU states it is subject to claims including 'infringement of intellectual property' (S002) and indemnification obligations for IP rights (S004). INTC faces similar claims from various entities including non-practicing entities, which can disrupt business and cause it to incur 'large costs to respond, defend, and resolve the claims' (P063_S001, P064_S002). Both companies highlight the defensive cost burden and operational disruption inherent in IP litigation.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks from IP protection and litigation costs
comparisons.peer_summary: Protecting IP rights and responding to infringement claims may result in substantial costs, damages, or discontinued product sales, and indemnifying customers may negatively impact operating results.
comparisons.comparison: MU and NVDA both identify intellectual property infringement as a key source of legal claims and highlight the financial burden of defending such actions or indemnifying customers. MU is subject to claims including IP infringement and has obligations to defend customers against third-party IP claims (S002, S004). NVDA is involved in lawsuits alleging patent infringement by itself or parties it has agreed to indemnify, and notes that such claims could cause it to incur 'significant costs to respond, defend, and resolve such claims' (P087_S001, P087_S003). Both emphasize the cost and indemnification aspects of IP risk.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risks of litigation and arbitration for IP enforcement
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm is currently engaged in litigation and may need to further litigate or arbitrate to enforce its rights, risking loss of patent enforcement ability, invalidation of license agreements, imposition of less favorable terms, and substantial costs. Enforcement actions can be costly, absorb management time, negatively impact results of operations and cash flows, and take significant time to conclude, reducing available revenues.
comparisons.comparison: MU and QCOM both disclose the risks and costs associated with litigation to enforce or defend intellectual property rights. MU faces claims of IP infringement and has indemnification obligations to defend customers against such claims (S002, S004). QCOM engages in litigation and arbitration to enforce its own IP rights or protect trade secrets, noting that such actions can be 'costly' and 'absorb significant management time' (P106_S001, P106_S003). While MU focuses on defending against claims and indemnifying others, QCOM focuses on actively enforcing rights, but both identify IP litigation as a significant source of cost and management distraction.
